web.title: Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M [2026]
web.description:
# Nigeria Tops Africa Startup Funding at $635M [2026]
## Nigeria Startup Funding Versus 2025: 2.6 Times the Money
The year-over-year comparison is the cleanest part of the data. Nigerian startups raised $247 million in January through September 2025 and $635 million in the same window of 2026. That is an increase of $388 million, or about 157%. [Nairametrics framed the result](https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/21/nigeria-reclaims-africas-startup-funding-lead-as-investments-rise-to-635-million/) as a rise in investment to $635 million, and several other Nigerian outlets used near-identical language on October 21.

The table below puts the two periods side by side. Averages in venture data run high when a few large rounds sit at the top.

## Egypt Closes In: $445 Million in Second Place
| Group (Jan-Sep 2026) | Amount raised | Share of Africa total (derived) |
|-|-|-|
| All African startups | about $2.16 billion | 100% |
| Nigeria | $635 million | about 29.4% |
| Egypt | $445 million | about 20.6% |
| Nigeria and Egypt combined | $1.08 billion | 50.0% |
| Moove, Flutterwave, Jumia, Yellow Card combined | $440 million | about 20.4% |
| Rest of Nigeria (73 ventures) | about $195 million | about 9.0% |
| All other markets and pan-African ventures | about $1.08 billion | 50.0% |

## Africa’s $2.16 Billion Total and the Wider Funding Climate
African startups collectively raised approximately **$2.16 billion** between January and September 2026. Nigeria’s $635 million is a strong result inside a continental total that is large but not explosive.

Global AI funding offers a useful yardstick for scale. Compare Nigeria’s total with the [$90 million seed round for a robot foundation-model startup](https://shattered.io/dream-labs-90m-seed-robot-foundation-model-2026/), which by itself represents about 14% of everything Nigerian startups raised in nine months.

That context frames Nigeria’s result. The country drew a total that beats its own prior-year number by 157%, even though the continental total is far smaller than the headline AI rounds elsewhere. [Business AM](https://businessamlive.com/nigeria-leads-africa-startup-funding-race-with-635m-in-nine-months/) and [MSME Africa](https://msmeafricaonline.com/nigerian-startups-raise-635m-in-nine-months-lead-africas-funding-market/) both led their coverage with the leadership angle, and The Whistler pointed to the inflow figure instead.

Advertisement

A funding story that quotes one tracker gives one view. Treat any single report, including this one, as a snapshot and not a verdict.

## FAQ: Nigeria Startup Funding in 2026
### How much did Nigerian startups raise in the first nine months of 2026?
Nigerian startups raised $635 million between January and September 2026, according to Africa: The Big Deal data cited by Nigerian and African outlets. Reports published on October 21 gave the figure.

### How does that compare with 2025?
The 2026 total is 2.6 times the $247 million raised in the same period of 2025. The number of ventures raising at least $100,000 rose from 70 to 77.

### Which companies raised the most?
Moove, Flutterwave, Jumia and Yellow Card together raised $440 million, about 69% of Nigeria’s total. The available reports do not give a confirmed amount for each company individually.

### How much did all of Africa raise?
African startups collectively raised approximately $2.16 billion between January and September 2026. Nigeria and Egypt together account for $1.08 billion, or half of that total.

### What does the funding mean for software developers?
Large rounds usually lead to more engineering hiring and more spending on cloud, security and developer tools. The reports reviewed do not give a separate funding figure for African developer-tools startups, so any such number should be treated as unverified.

### What does Africa: The Big Deal track?
The tracker monitors African startups that raise at least $100,000.
